purpose: Preserve platform relation, intended addressee, and semantic content as distinct channels. A correctly recognized symbol does not certify that the relation in which it occurs was correctly bound.
source_note: Anonymized from a user-provided conversational trace. Intent is supplied as an explicit annotation rather than inferred by the witness.

certifies: The platform reply target differs from the explicitly declared intended addressee.
The explicit textual addressee matches the declared intended addressee.
does_not_certify: Why the author made the binding error.
What the author believed about the quoted message before replying.
Whether the platform UI caused the error.
Whether any actor had authority over another actor.
Any downstream causal influence on the agent.

required_behavior: Keep speaker, platform reply target, textual addressee, and intended addressee in separate fields.
Classify role_misbinding only from explicit relation mismatch plus explicit addressee agreement.
Treat declared intent as an input annotation, not a mechanically inferred fact.
forbidden_behavior: Collapse platform reply target and intended addressee into a single recipient field.
Infer the author's cognitive cause from the mismatch alone.
Treat semantic recognition of the word Agent as proof that conversational role binding was correct.

minimal_pair.invariant: Symbol recognition does not imply relation recognition or correct operation.

falsification: If platform_reply_target equals intended_addressee, the witness must not classify role_misbinding.
If explicit_text_addressee does not match intended_addressee, the witness must return unresolved rather than invent the intended relation.
If intended_addressee is absent, the witness must return unresolved.
srv_rule: signal recognized does not entail role bound; role bound does not entail authorized operation
chalked_rule: Preserve the relation as evidence. Do not let fluent semantic interpretation overwrite who addressed whom.
